3.0.0.en: The Apostle James was bishop of Jerusalem and one of the pillars of the Church, and yet he says in humility, “Be not many masters, my brethren,” because he found that some were competing to take on the image of the teacher and guide, and so put themselves in danger, for the following reasons:

3.0.1.en: (1) Because it gives him a false sense that he is better than others.

3.0.2.en: (2) Because teaching is in essence a gift of the Holy Spirit, so no one should seize it by his pride. (3) Every teacher receives a greater condemnation, because what he teaches he must first do himself.

3.0.3.en: (4) “Unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required” (Lk 12:48). (5) Every teacher is exposed to falling, and when Satan makes him fall he scatters the flock. Therefore we find that Arius, who was a skilled orator and went astray, caused many to fall after him.

3.1.0.en: Every person is exposed to falling into sin, and no one can completely control his tongue except the Perfect One, who is Christ. Whoever controls his tongue can control all his lusts, thoughts and senses. And since a person strives and controls himself to some extent by the grace of God, he should be careful not to rush into teaching others.

3.1.1.en: Let us therefore take heed in everything we learn and also in what we do. For this reason every person must have a wise father of confession to be a guide for him so that his spiritual life may be set straight, and instead of teaching others, he should first be concerned with the salvation of his own soul, because the war against those who serve is fierce.

3.2.0.en: The Apostle likens the tongue to three things:

3.2.1.en: 1- The first comparison: he likens the tongue to the bit that is put in the mouths of horses so that the rider may steer them in the direction he wants, because if horses had no bit they would throw and destroy their rider. In the same way, whoever controls his tongue can move his whole body, that is, his conduct, in the way of truth, so that the body does not break loose in its lusts like a horse without a bit.

3.2.2.en: Let us train ourselves to control the tongue so that by the grace of Christ we may be able to control the lusts of the body.

3.3.0.en: The second comparison: he likens the tongue to the rudder of a ship, which, though small, lets the helmsman steer a huge ship in the direction he wants, however strong the winds. In the same way the tongue is a small member that we must handle with care in every word we utter, “for by your words you shall be justified, and by your words you shall be condemned” (Mt 12:37). The tongue can defile the whole body and bring judgment on us, though on the other hand it is able to lead a person in peace like the rudder of a ship.

3.4.0.en: The third comparison: he likens the tongue to a spark, that is, a small fire that can kindle huge fires.

3.4.1.en: Just as a small spark kindles huge fires, so with one word from the tongue fire is kindled in the world of sin and iniquity, and divisions, hatred and enmity arise among people.

3.4.2.en: And it setteth on fire: that is, it kindles wars among peoples. The tongue boasts, exalting itself, that it directs the whole universe, and it leads a person to pride and so defiles the whole body, because it brings many evils and then casts the whole body into hell.

3.4.3.en: Hell (Gehenna): named after the valley of “Hinnom”, which lies southeast of the Temple, below Jerusalem. The blood of sacrifices flowed into it, and the Jews threw into it dead animals and refuse to burn them, so the fires in it were not quenched night and day; hence it is used to refer to the eternal fire.

3.5.0.en: The fourth comparison: he likens it to poison, because it is easy for a person to tame wild beasts, birds or reptiles, but the insolent tongue that is accustomed to foul speech is hard to tame, though God can of course do so. Sometimes the tongue utters a word, and it comes out like the deadly venom of a serpent and destroys a relationship that took many years to build. Therefore David says in the Psalm, “Set a watch, O Lord, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips” (Ps 141:3).

3.5.1.en: If your tongue affects the salvation of your soul and your relationships with those around you to this degree, may you not rush into speaking, so that you give yourself an opportunity to seek God and to listen attentively to those around you, and God will guide you to the fitting words.

3.6.0.en: The Apostle rebukes those who curse others: how can they bless God with their tongue in prayers and then trouble people created in the image of God with their bad words? What are they doing: are they blessing God or cursing Him?!

3.6.1.en: And he declares that this is a grave error that should never be.

3.7.0.en: The fifth comparison: he likens the tongue to a spring of water, and asks whether it is possible for the same spring to send forth two kinds of water, one sweet and the other bitter?! This is a rhetorical question, meaning that this cannot happen, and therefore it is not right for prayers and bad words to come out of the same tongue. Thus the Apostle James calls us to repent of bad speech.

3.8.0.en: The sixth comparison: he likens it to a tree, and asks a second rhetorical question: can a tree bear fruit contrary to its kind?! Can a fig tree, for example, bear olives, or a vine figs?! Of course not. So the tongue of the children of God must speak only words of blessing, whether to God in prayers or to people in kind speech.

3.8.1.en: Because you are a child of God, this must show in your speech with others, in kind words, whether in encouragement, or in apologizing for your mistakes and showing your readiness to help them and cooperate with them, so that you offer the love of God that is in you through your good words.

3.9.0.en: He speaks to the believers who want to teach others and says to them: whoever among you has wisdom, knowledge and learning, so as to teach another, must show his wisdom in two ways:

3.9.1.en: 1- Sound conduct in the various situations of life, for how can you teach others wisdom while you act in an unsound way?

3.9.2.en: 2- That his sound conduct be accompanied by meekness, that is, calm of heart, and likewise by not being disturbed in his dealings with others.

3.10.0.en: Glory not, and lie not against the truth: do not think of yourselves that you are wise teachers when you are fallen into sin, and you have human knowledge and wisdom far from God and the truth.

3.10.1.en: The Apostle draws a comparison between earthly wisdom and heavenly wisdom. Earthly wisdom springs from love of the world, so that brother tramples on brother for the sake of money, and it is “sensual”, that is, it comes from the human self (the ego), like teachings that take a religious form and have an emotional effect and suggest holiness and piety to the soul, but are far from spiritual things. The true saint, however, always feels that he is a sinner and in need of repentance the nearer he comes to the divine throne, like the prophet Isaiah. The spiritual life usually has no violent leaps, but grows gradually like a plant, or like a child: when you give him a meal he does not grow up suddenly, but grows day by day.

3.10.2.en: Earthly wisdom is also “devilish”, that is, its hidden motive is Satan, who suggests to a person that he alone is wise, and so brings into him the spirit of pride and envy, and divisions, confusion, deviations, factions and partiality arise, and heresies come into being under the cover of this wisdom.

3.11.0.en: Heavenly wisdom is given by God to whoever asks in faith, not wavering, and its characteristics are:

3.11.1.en: 1- Pure: that is, clean, with no crooked purpose, far from partiality; its possessor practices a pure religion that shows in visiting widows and orphans.

3.11.2.en: 2- Peaceable: because its source is the King of peace, and not as the world gives a temporary peace; it is peacemaking, so peace and calm spread between a person and himself, between him and God, and between him and people.

3.11.3.en: 3- Gentle: toward the mistakes of others, it embraces them, bears their weakness and encourages them to repent, like the gentleness of Christ and His encouragement of Zacchaeus the chief of the tax collectors (Lk 19:1-10) and of the sinful woman in the house of Simon the Pharisee (Lk 7:36-50).

3.11.4.en: 4- Easy to be entreated: this means readiness to obey the divine commandment, the Church and parents, as it is said of Christ that He was subject to His mother the Virgin and Joseph the carpenter (Lk 2:51); it also listens to others, but with discernment, without being led or yielding to mistaken opinions.

3.11.5.en: 5- Full of mercy and good fruits: heavenly wisdom bears fruits of mercy and good works toward the weak, sinners, the needy, the poor, the sick and the fainthearted, resting on living faith that works by love.

3.11.6.en: 6- Without partiality: that is, firm in the love of God and faith in Him, far from doubt and wavering.

3.11.7.en: 7- Without hypocrisy: that is, what is inside the heart is what appears on a person in his conduct and behavior.

3.11.8.en: 8- The fruit of righteousness: heavenly wisdom sows peace, so it bears righteousness and good, pure works.

3.11.9.en: May we humble ourselves before God and others and ask Him for wisdom, and He will teach us how to act and speak with those around us, keeping purity and repentance, so that He may continue to work in us by His Holy Spirit and give us His wisdom. Evil desires

4.0.0.en: Your lusts that war in your members: the evil desires that draw the members of the body to the pleasure of sin.

4.0.1.en: Evil desires cause serious results in a person’s life, the most important of which are:

4.0.2.en: (1) Problems between people: the desires of sin make people differ with one another and clash, because they produce selfishness in the heart and so cause quarrels and problems, even violent wars, between people.

4.1.0.en: Because ye ask not: you do not seek God and the spiritual life with Him.

4.1.1.en: (2) Never being satisfied: the evil desires that produce selfishness in a person make him greedy, so he runs after desires and uses every means of evil, such as sins of the flesh, quarreling and murder, but he is not satisfied with his desire; rather his thirst for it increases, like one who runs after a mirage and is never quenched but is lost in the wilderness of the world, because he does not seek God and spiritual things but only his material desires, which increase his thirst.

4.2.0.en: (3) Corruption of the relationship with God: the Apostle shows that indulgence in desires corrupts the relationship with God, for their prayers turn toward material requests and leave the love of God and of others, and therefore God does not answer them, and they receive nothing of what they asked, because they ask for their evil desires.

4.3.1.en: The Holy Bible likens God’s relationship with His people to the bond of a bridegroom with his bride and counts the believer’s love of the world as spiritual adultery, so it declares plainly that it is enmity with God, because it takes a person away from Him, and he is occupied with love of the world, which should have been only a bridge to cross over to the heavenly wedding. God asks us for love with all our hearts, as a husband who expects from his bride her whole heart. Therefore the Apostle Paul says, “For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ” (2 Cor 11:2); that is, every person has freedom of will to choose either to love God and hate the world, or to love the world and hate God.

4.4.0.en: The spirit that dwelleth in us: the Holy Spirit who dwelt in us in the sacrament of the Holy Myron.

4.4.1.en: Lusteth to envy: He loves us and is jealous over us because of the devil’s dominion, and strives to return us to His love. Whoever loves the world and clings to material things is an enemy of God. The whole Holy Bible declares God’s love for us and His jealousy over us, and the Holy Spirit who dwelt in us in the sacrament of the Holy Myron is jealous over us if we cling to desires and material things. He does not stand against us if we are hostile to Him, but in His love He wants to bring us back to Him and deliver us from the grip of the devil, and even gives us grace to resist the wars of Satan, and then gives us the enjoyment of peace, joy and delight in His fellowship.

4.5.0.en: 5- Pride: desires produce pride, which makes a person increase in desires, lose the grace of God and resist Him, so that He is angry with him for his stubbornness. On the other hand, whoever humbles himself before God, He delivers him from his sins and gives him the enjoyment of His fellowship.

4.5.1.en: If you are fought by any desire, humble yourself before God in repentance and humility so that He may remove it from you, and do not be troubled however much you fall, but persevere in your striving and be careful to keep away from the sources of these desires.

4.6.0.en: Humility and submission to God by obeying His commandments support a person with strength to resist the wars of the devil so that he does not fear him, but on the contrary the devil fears the power of God and keeps away from this striving person.

4.7.0.en: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you: draw near to God by prayer, by reading His holy word and by partaking of the Holy Mysteries; then you will feel His nearness to you, for He is near to you, and your drawing near to Him is a response to His love, and then you will feel that He draws near to you, and you will enjoy His care and providence more than before.

4.7.1.en: Cleanse your hands, ye sinners: by repenting of your sins, which show in your conduct and works, indicated by the hands.

4.7.2.en: Purify your hearts, ye double minded: you who waver between love of the world and love of God, be purified from this wavering and reject love of the world, so that you may be of one mind, which is love of God.

4.7.3.en: He calls them to prayer, to reading the Holy Bible and to repentance of sins, so that they may walk in the love of God.

4.8.0.en: He calls them to deep repentance with contrition and tears, in distress over sin, instead of indulging in the joys of desires, their corrupt pleasures and their wicked laughter.

4.9.0.en: If they feel the horror of their sins they will repent in humility, asking for God’s help and forgiveness, and to the extent that they humble themselves before Him, He removes their sins from them and blesses them, and even glorifies them and gives them the enjoyment of His love.

4.10.0.en: The Apostle forbids them to judge, because it is not only against the one they judge but also against the Law, which commands love of neighbor. Whoever judges breaks the Law and becomes opposed to it, that is, it condemns him because of his deeds, which are the judging of another.

4.11.0.en: God is the giver of the Law, and He alone is the Judge of the whole world. How then do you dare, O man, to judge another? By this you usurp the place of God the Judge and expose yourself to His judgment and punishment, for God in His mercy is able to lead your brothers who have fallen into sin so that they are saved, while you perish because of your insistence on judging.

4.11.1.en: Be concerned with your own repentance, and make excuses for those who sin around you, and to the extent of your humility before God His mercies will overflow upon you. Be positive and concerned with your repentance and your striving against sin, and as for others who fall into sin like you, pray for them, that God may have mercy on you and on them.

4.12.0.en: He rebukes those who rely on their own strength and are occupied with love of money, who go from place to place for trade and profit without relying on God. Trade is not wrong in itself, but not relying on God is the wrong.

4.13.0.en: He warns them that they do not know when their life will end, because the life of man is short, and he likens it to vapor, which appears large in shape but quickly vanishes. Therefore one should seize the opportunity of life to repent of the love of money and of all sins and to care for the salvation of the soul; and as for the works of the world, one should rely on God in them, and God should remain the only goal of life.

4.14.0.en: The Apostle here makes clear the sound conduct, which is to rely on God and then to practice any work or trade. Prayer is essential before beginning any work.

4.15.0.en: He also rebukes their pride and their boasting in their strength and their money, for this pride is evil and rejected by God, and even brings His wrath upon men.

4.16.0.en: Lest some become lazy about working, he warns us of the importance of doing all good duties, for everything good and useful must be committed to, whether in material or spiritual works, relying on God in them, and every opportunity to do good should be seized, because life is short and will quickly end, and since God has given us the opportunity to work, how can we neglect it?! Work is a blessing because it is for God’s sake and not a heavy duty, and wasting opportunities for work is counted a sin for which a person is held to account before God.

4.16.1.en: Be concerned not only to keep away from evil but also to do good and seize every opportunity to encourage and support those around you; and if you were negligent, offer repentance for that before your father of confession, and then rise to seize new opportunities to do good.
